ct_chin_the.blurb: The Chin is the most prominent cliff inside Sleeping Giant State Park in Hamden, Connecticut. Around sixteen routes, almost all traditional with a few that can also be top-roped, run from easy fifth-class lines up through low 5.11, with the bulk between 5.5 and 5.9. The face looks east and catches the early morning sun. The stone is abrasive and can be loose in places, any old fixed protection should be treated as untrustworthy, and poison ivy grows thickly around the base. Expect an older-style, run-it-out feel rather than a polished sport crag.

ct_llama_s_skull.blurb: Llama's Skull is a compact cluster of granite boulders beside the Branford trail near Stony Creek, within the Westwoods section of Cockaponset State Forest. It holds sixteen problems, and the grades stay friendly: a few at V0 and V1, a solid middle of V2 and V3, and a single V4. Reaching the boulders takes only about half a minute of walking once you pass beneath the railway bridge and turn right. It sits just up the path from the much harder Bunny Boulder, so it makes a good low-key stop for newer boulderers or a warm-up before the bigger lines.

ct_gollum_s_playground.blurb: Gollum's Playground is a bouldering zone in Case Mountain's forested trail network in Manchester, Connecticut. It lists sixteen problems from V0 up to a handful in the V5 to V8 range, with the middle weighted toward V1 and V3. A tall, near-vertical wall in three sections carries thin horizontal cracks, while a cave-like overhanging wall at a right angle to it offers crimps, side-pulls and big flakes. A smaller quartz-veined wall adds a few more lines. The rock is coarse with sharp holds and some smoother, softer ones, and a few loose flakes low down are worth testing. Plenty of unclimbed potential remains.

ct_bunny_boulder_the.blurb: The Bunny Boulder is one large, high-quality granite block shaped like a rabbit, sitting right beside a trail in the Westwoods part of Cockaponset State Forest near Stony Creek, Connecticut. It has sixteen problems, and unlike most boulders in the state it is a hard-climber's stop: a few easy lines and some V4 to V7 problems, then several at V9 and V10 and one around V11. A few very hard lines remain unclimbed. The landings are described as decent on every side, and the walk from the car is only a few minutes.
